defects_found_and_fixed.found: A completely untouched, fresh form read "2% filled in" instead of 0%, because updateProgress() counted the two K13-prefilled values (hall_website_url, allergy_policy) as "answered" even though the client hadn't touched them yet, inconsistent with the rest of the form's own fieldIsUntouchedPrefill logic used for section ticks and the still-open panel.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: updateProgress() now excludes untouched-prefill fields from the filled count, matching sectionHasRealContent()'s existing rule.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: Fresh load now reads exactly "0% filled in".

defects_found_and_fixed.found: renderVendors() rebuilds every one of the 15 vendor cards from scratch on ANY hall-default keystroke, any override toggle, and any bulk action, and always started every rebuilt card collapsed. So a vendor card Lorena had open to review would snap shut on her the moment she typed one more character into a hall-default field, clicked an override toggle, or ran a bulk action.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: renderVendors() now records which vendor cards were open before the rebuild (by a new data-vendor-id attribute) and reopens the same ones after, instead of always starting every card collapsed.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: An expanded vendor card now survives typing in a hall-default field, clicking its own override toggle, and running a bulk action.

defects_found_and_fixed.area: Keyboard accessibility — chip checkboxes/radios and toggle switches
defects_found_and_fixed.found: The real checkbox/radio inside every chip and every toggle switch is visually hidden (opacity:0), and the form's generic input:focus rule explicitly sets outline:none on all inputs including these. Verified with real Tab-key navigation that a keyboard user got zero visible indication of which control was focused.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added label.chip:has(input:focus-visible) and .switch:has(input:focus-visible) rules that put a visible teal focus ring on the label/switch itself.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: Real Tab navigation now lands a visible solid 2px teal outline on both chip labels and switches.

defects_found_and_fixed.found: The Opening/Closing time <select> dropdowns (generated in JS) had no accessible name at all.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: renderTimeChoice()/initTimeChoices() now set aria-label="Opening time" / "Closing time" on the generated selects.

defects_found_and_fixed.found: 10 static fields, the hall-default "Can connect calls here" switch, and every vendor's own transfer-override switch (15x) and Notes field (15x) had no accessible name; 41 nodes total. passes.verdict: PASS after two real fixes. Found and fixed the storage-quota area's two genuine failure modes (a silent, easy-to-miss autosave failure, and an undetected-photo-format fallback that could itself exhaust the quota). Found and fixed a real data-loss bug in Load Backup. Everything else attacked (messy input, double-clicks, cancel flows, reload mid-typing, two sittings via a real browser close) held up with no console/page errors and no silent data loss. Safe to send to Lorena.

defects_found_and_fixed.area: Vendor photo upload, undecodable image fallback
defects_found_and_fixed.severity: high (the exact storage-exhaustion scenario the brief asked to hunt for)
defects_found_and_fixed.found: processLogoFile() downscales an uploaded photo to a small 220px JPEG before storing it, but if the browser's element fails to decode the file (img.onerror), the old code fell back to callback(reader.result), the FULL, UN-downscaled original as a base64 data URL. Reproduced directly: a 236KB synthetic iPhone-style HEIC photo (Chromium cannot decode HEIC) landed in localStorage as a 322KB raw data URL instead of a small JPEG, and the on-screen logo also just silently failed to render (broken image, no message). A real iPhone HEIC photo (commonly 1.5-4MB at full resolution) would do this at full size; two or three such photos across the 15 vendor cards would alone exceed this browser's measured ~4-5MB file:// storage quota, taking every other answer down with it since doSave() writes one combined payload.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: processLogoFile() now calls back with null on any decode/processing failure instead of the raw original. The upload handler checks for null and shows a clear toast ("That photo couldn't be used, this often happens with iPhone photos saved as HEIC, please pick a JPG or PNG instead...") without touching vd.logo, so a failed photo leaves the vendor exactly where it was (placeholder/hint text intact) instead of silently bloating storage with something that wasn't even going to display.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: Re-ran the same HEIC upload: no data stored for that vendor's logo, toast shown, no console errors. Re-ran 15 real JPEG uploads afterward to confirm no regression (still ~112KB total, all render correctly).

defects_found_and_fixed.severity: high (exactly the brief's core concern: "never lose her work without telling her")
defects_found_and_fixed.found: doSave()'s catch block on a failed localStorage.setItem (quota exceeded, private-mode restrictions, etc.) only changed a small text label inside the sticky statusbar's corner ("Could not autosave in this browser, use Download backup instead"). No toast, no visual color change on the save-status dot, no banner. A careless real user is very likely to keep typing for the rest of a sitting believing autosave is on, then close the tab and lose everything typed since the failure, with zero warning she'd actually notice.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added a persistent, styled warning banner (role="alert", using the brand's existing --danger token, matches the form's visual system) that appears in the statusbar the moment a save fails and stays until a save succeeds again; the save-status dot turns red and pulses (gated behind prefers-reduced-motion); a one-time toast fires on the failing transition (not spammed every 500ms while she keeps typing); the banner has its own "Download backup now" button wired to the same in-memory-state-based download used elsewhere, so it keeps working even while localStorage itself is unusable. Clears itself automatically, with a confirming toast, the moment a save succeeds again.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: Forced a deterministic quota failure (monkeypatched setItem) to test the UI logic in isolation from this machine's specific quota size: banner + red pulsing dot appear immediately, the banner's download button produces a complete correct backup with the just-typed value, and everything clears cleanly once the forced failure is removed and typing resumes. Screenshots: docs/intake/qa/12-storage-full-banner-desktop.png, docs/intake/qa/13-storage-full-banner-mobile.png.

defects_found_and_fixed.area: Load Backup — wrong-shape file silently destroys current progress
defects_found_and_fixed.found: The "Load backup" handler did JSON.parse(file) then immediately localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(data)) and loadState() with NO shape validation and NO confirmation dialog (unlike "Clear this form", which does confirm). Picking any valid-JSON-but-wrong-shape file (an empty object, a random JSON file, an array) silently wiped everything currently on screen back to blank defaults, overwrote the real saved answers in localStorage with the bad file's contents, and still showed "Backup loaded, your answers have been restored", a false success message for what was actually silent data destruction. There was also no confirmation before overwriting current work even for a genuinely valid backup, so a stray double-click or picking the wrong .json file by mistake had no safety net at all.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: The file is now validated (object shape, has at least one of vendors/faqs/fields) BEFORE anything is written to localStorage or applied to state; an invalid file shows a clear, honest error and changes nothing. A valid-looking file now asks for confirmation ("Load this backup? Everything currently in the form will be replaced...") before applying, matching the existing pattern used by "Clear this form". The actual apply step is also wrapped in try/catch so an unexpected runtime error during restore reports itself instead of throwing silently.
defects_found_and_fixed.verified: Re-tested a non-JSON file, an empty-object JSON file, and a bare-array JSON file: all three now leave the original in-progress answer ("ORIGINAL VALUE, must survive bad loads") completely untouched and show a clear message. A genuinely valid backup file still round-trips correctly, now behind one confirm() prompt. No console errors on any path.

residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.topic: The last ~500ms of typing before a reload/crash
residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.what: Autosave is debounced 500ms after the last keystroke or change event. Reloading, closing, or crashing inside that window loses only what was typed in that window, confirmed empirically, no corruption, no error, no loss of anything already saved.
residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.why_left_alone: This is the same debounce window every autosave pattern like this uses; shrinking it further trades save-storm risk (more localStorage churn, closer to the quota) for a marginal reduction in an already-tiny loss window. Not worth changing without Kazim asking for it.

residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.topic: file:// localStorage quota is small and possibly shared across unrelated local HTML files
residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.what: Empirically measured this browser's file:// origin quota at roughly 4-5MB, noticeably tighter than a typical https origin. Chromium's file:// storage bucketing (whether it's per-file-path or shared machine-wide across all file:// pages) was not fully characterized, out of scope for a fix inside this one file since it's browser behavior, not something the form controls.
residual_risk_noted_not_fixed.why_left_alone: The form-side mitigation (loud warning + a download path that works regardless of localStorage state, from Defect #2) is the right fix at this layer. Real-world usage (text answers + normal JPEG/PNG photos) measured well under quota in testing (~112KB for 15 real photos), so this is a defense-in-depth fix for an edge case, not a fix for an everyday failure.
